title: Artie Shaw wakes him up to the clarinet
summary: Holmes liked Buster Bailey but no other clarinetists until he heard Artie Shaw at the Paramount, whom he preferred to Benny Goodman.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Oh, he was a great clarinetist. But I didn't know... I wasn't interested in clarinet. I never learned clarinet. I didn't like clarinet until I heard Artie Shaw play it. No, I heard Buster Bailey. I liked him. I liked Buster. But the rest of the clarinet players I didn't like, until I heard Artie Shaw; and Artie Shaw woke me up. And it looked like the next week... Let me see, I heard him at the Paramount, and it looked like the following week or two or whatever, Artie's date.... Then Benny coming in -- Benny Goodman. He followed Artie in there. I was comparing the two of them. I said I'll still take Artie. Because Artie was playing... He was articulating way up on the clarinet -- way up. Hard stuff, you know. But Benny was swingin'. Benny was just swingin'. I mean, he could play, but he was swingin'. But Artie was thinkin' hard stuff to play. Boy, I mean, I was thrilled at it.
And then when Artie passed out the picture, when I heard him speak on the air one night about, well, you know, it's not so great being number two...
